title: Autotune: default batching/caching, quant profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Khan
description: Context: we've seen customer reports and internal benchmarks that suboptimal default batching and caching settings increase per-token costs for short responses and increase tail latency for chat workloads. This PR implements: 1) a new autotune-based defaults subsystem that chooses batching and prefix/KV caching defaults based on deployment profile (hosted/dedicated/private), model class, and observed request size distribution; 2) a curated set of quantization profiles (int8/int4 variants) with validation matrices per model family to enable safe defaults for CPU/GPU-serving; 3) a lightweight unit-economics CLI and dashboard hooks that compute per-route unit costs given current defaults and expected workload distribution. Motivation: give customers immediate cost gains without manual tuning, and provide ops teams with visibility into how defaults impact unit economics. What this PR changes: - runtime/autotune: new autotune service that samples request histograms, runs candidate configs in a sandbox, and promotes configurations when SLOs are met. - runtime/batching: switch default policy to adaptive with a new default windowing strategy and backpressure thresholds tuned for chat workloads. - runtime/cache: introduce per-route prefix/KV cache policies and a new safe-fallback for short-lived sessions. - models/quant-profiles.yaml: add vetted quant profiles for LlamaX, Redys-13B, and mosaic*. Profiles include fallback/resolution rules and supported hw. - tooling/uecon: CLI (uecon estimate) and backend hooks to emit per-route unit cost metrics and wire to console dashboards. - docs: quickstart and migration notes for Dedicated and Private customers. Testing and validation: - microbenchmarks across G5/G4/CPU showed mean token cost reduction of 12-22% for small-response workloads and unchanged latency for long-running generation. - staging rollout: gradual rollout on non-critical tenants for 72 hours, with automated rollback on 5% SLA degradation. - CI: unit + integration tests added for autotune simulation and quant-profile parsing. Rollout plan: canary on staged tenants -> 2-week prod canary on low-traffic regions -> global rollout behind feature flag. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-3145) - [x] unit/integration tests - [x] bench results attached - [x] docs updated - [x] console UI hook wired - [x] rollout plan and rollback criteria included Notes: this PR intentionally keeps configuration promotion conservative (requires 3 consecutive evaluation windows with SLO pass). Follow-ups: add per-customer sensitivity tuning and an opt-out API for enterprise tenants.
